description.narrative: Gemensamfinansierat program hanterat av UNDP (executing agency). Målet är att minska Bangladesh sårbarhet för naturliga och antropogenfaror, inklusive förutsedda effekter av klimatförändringarna. Total budget 70 MUSD. Övriga givare är DfID, EU, Norge, Australien och UNDP. Ministry of Food and Disaster management är ansvarigt ministerium. Bygger på CDMP fas 1 2004-2009. Ingår i Sveriges särsilda klimatsatsning.

Pool funded program managed by UNDP. Ministry of Food and Disaster Management is responsible ministry and Disaster Management Bureau implementing agency for Govt of Bangl. Objective is to reduce the vulnerability of Bangladesh for natural and antropogenic hazards, including effects of climate change. Total budget 70 MUSD. Other Dps DfID, EU, Norway; Aus and UNDP. CDMP1 previous phase. Part of SW CCI.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2015Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: During the six year period since the start of the second phase (2010 up to end 2015) CDMP has contributed to significant improvement of disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation in Bangladesh. The programme has become a model and example of disaster management programming and have received international praise. CDMP II programming as covered virtually every aspect of DRR and CCA and this ambitious scope has sometimes spread interventions thinly and caused delays in implementation. Because of these delays the programme was accorded a one year extension. The additional year, postponing operational closure to December 2015, has allowed an orderly closure of activities and has been focused on legacy and sustainability of the programme results. Major results related to the intended outcomes are summarized below: -The National Disaster Management Act was enacted in 2012 by the parliament. -DRR & CCA have been integrated in educational curricula of 17 universities and 11 training intuitions. -3.48 million people have benefited from risk reduction schemes in 312 Union Parisahads. -195 Disaster Management Committees were trained on disaster management issues in different hazard zones of the country. -Interactive Voice Response- based early warning systems are accessible for 126 million cell phone users in Bangladesh. -More than 50000 volunteers were trained on cyclone and flood preparedness.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
